test_title: PYST 27: RRB Group D - GS (Held On: 09 Dec, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
A ball of mass 3 kg is raised to a height of 6 m. Its potential energy is _______.

Take g = 10 { m/s}²
solution:
The correct answer is __**180 J**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **potential energy** of an object is the energy possessed by it by virtue of its **position or configuration**. In this specific case, it refers to **gravitational potential energy**, which is the energy an object possesses due to its height above the ground.
 
• The mathematical formula used to calculate gravitational potential energy is **P.E. = m × g × h**, where **m** represents the **mass** of the object, **g** is the **acceleration due to gravity**, and **h** is the **height** or displacement from the reference point.
 
• In the given problem, the **mass (m)** of the ball is **3 kg** and it is raised to a **height (h)** of **6 m**. The value of **acceleration due to gravity (g)** is provided as **10 m/s²**.
 
• By substituting the values into the formula: **P.E. = 3 kg × 10 m/s² × 6 m**. This yields a total of **180**.
 
• The **SI unit** of energy is the **Joule (J)**, named after the English physicist **James Prescott Joule**. Therefore, the calculated potential energy is **180 J**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Kinetic Energy (K.E.):** Unlike potential energy, **Kinetic Energy** is the energy possessed by an object due to its **motion**. It is calculated using the formula **K.E. = 1/2 mv²**, where **v** is the **velocity** of the object.
 
• **Mechanical Energy:** The sum total of the **potential energy** and **kinetic energy** of an object is referred to as its total **Mechanical Energy**. According to the **Law of Conservation of Energy**, energy can neither be created nor destroyed; it can only be transformed from one form to another.
 
• **Elastic Potential Energy:** This is another form of potential energy stored as a result of applying a force to deform an elastic object, such as a **compressed spring** or a **stretched rubber band**. The energy is stored until the force is removed and the object returns to its original shape.
 
• **Work-Energy Theorem:** This principle states that the **net work done** on an object is equal to the **change in its kinetic energy**. When work is done to raise an object against gravity, that work is stored as **gravitational potential energy**.
 
• **Units and Dimensions:** Energy has the same **SI unit** as **work**, which is the **Joule**. In terms of base units, **1 Joule** is equal to **1 kg·m²/s²**. The dimensional formula for energy is **[ML²T²]**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Mass vs. Weight:** It is important to distinguish between **mass (3 kg)** and **weight**. Weight is a force equal to **mass multiplied by gravity (m × g)**. In this problem, the weight of the ball is **30 Newtons (N)**.
 
• **Reference Level:** Potential energy is always relative to a **reference level** (usually the ground). If the reference level changes, the calculated value of **potential energy** will also change, although the **change in potential energy** remains the same.
 
• **Acceleration due to Gravity:** While **g** is often approximated as **10 m/s²** for calculation ease in competitive exams, its standard value on **Earth** is approximately **9.8 m/s²**. On the **Moon**, the value of **g** is about **1.62 m/s²**, which significantly reduces the potential energy of the same object at the same height.
 
• **Scalar Quantity:** Energy is a **scalar quantity**, meaning it has **magnitude** but no **direction**, unlike force or velocity which are vector quantities.
